title: Term-structure models and rate risk
acceptance: Recommendation to coordinator only; canonical acceptance, shared integration and publication remain root-owned.
independence: Read the entire frozen chapter, README, inputs, analysis, reference output, manifest, author checker/review and source proposals. scope.proofs: Finite self-financing bank-numeraire martingale/no-arbitrage; positive shape calibration existence and conditional uniqueness; local P-SDF covariance identity; forward harmonic-mean inequality; finite AR moments; two-state replication and rank.
scope.instruction: All required methods are taught locally or rely on explicit accepted finite-state prerequisites. Four worked cases, ten ordered prompt/solution pairs, research critique criteria, answered committee teach-back and delayed retention are complete. No Brownian/Ito or continuous-time option result is assumed.

proof_and_model_audit: At each node d is known before the next interval; the coupon and continuation are discounted together once. Ex-payment conventions and date-1 sale of a date-2 zero are consistent with the stated claim.

A predictable signed strategy in consistently priced assets, including distributions, has discounted self-financing wealth with constant conditional Q expectation. Finite states/finite positions ensure integrability; strict common P/Q support and strictly positive bank wealth exclude the stated arbitrage. This does not prove completeness.

Bank accumulation is history dependent even at a recombining rate node. LH and HL Arrow contributions remain separate before aggregation; normalized Arrow weights need not equal the bank-numeraire Q probabilities.

The fitted level is positive and unique conditional on chosen positive shape and conditional Q, with all earlier prices unchanged. The s bound is tied to the three-period fixture. Fitting initial discount points does not identify dispersion, physical beliefs or unique contingent-claim prices.

The physical return identity uses a positive local m=dq/p and the actual purchase price; the covariance relation was recomputed using the independent two-state difference formula. The forward combines next gross rates harmonically and need not equal even the Q mean.

The additive mean-reversion iteration and variance use independent centered unit-variance shocks. The phi=1 boundary is discussed through the finite sum; the physical example is not represented as fitted Q dynamics. A finite square-root step can leave its state domain, and clamping changes its mean.

The contingent hedge uses the distinct successor-price determinant and explicitly funds date-1 bank repayment. Equal successor prices at zero dispersion admit the stated bank-only replica for this equal-payoff claim. The manuscript does not infer universal replication from two arbitrarily chosen assets.
Negative rates above minus one are admissible only within the stated opportunity set. Adding outside costless storage supplies a new conditional arbitrage; it is not assumed in the original model.

Curve-coordinate recalibration derivatives are distinct from future-node hedge holdings. Both payoff boundaries and the invalid negative linear extrapolation are correct. Pricing scenarios carry no unstated physical occurrence law.

Source-based research critique correctly separates calibration residuals, physical forecasts, premium conventions and held-out hedge evidence. All five memo claims have substantive answers and the rubric permits defensible alternative validation designs.

validation.independent_methods: Direct three-period shape moments solve levels; full history ledgers produce zeros, coupon prices, Arrow weights, P/Q probabilities and path SDFs; determinant hedge system funds date-1 cash; two-state covariance formula and explicitly rebalanced wealth ledger; finite innovation sums derive AR moments.

limits: This is an independent specialist computational/editorial review, not external human certification.
Synthetic finite models are conditionally coherent; the review does not establish real-world P/Q estimates, empirical performance or universal hedge implementability.
Shared full-library build, dependency-order acceptance and visual/mobile/keyboard/print QA remain coordinator/library gates.
